title: Citrine Retail — POC kickoff: KV caching & unit-econ scoping
summary: Initial POC scoping to validate per-token economics and latency for Citrine's product search augmentation. Discussed benchmark plan, sample workload, batching and KV prefix caching knobs, target SLOs and a 6-week pilot timeline. Agreed next steps: share benchmark template, provide access to lightweight containerized runner, schedule deep-dive with infra team.
topics: per-token cost estimates and target budget
bench plan: datasets, metrics, and success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Maria Santos: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick intro from our side, I'm Maria, AE on the account, Devon my SE will lead the bench plan.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Hey Maria, Samir here. We're really hoping to validate that we can hit sub-200ms p95 for search assistant and that the per-token cost fits our runway.
[00:22] Devon Clarke: great, Samir. quick question to ground the numbers: what does your traffic look like? qps, concurrency, average prompt/completion lengths?
[00:30] Laura Chen: rough estimates: peak qps around 250, sustained 80 qps. typical user prompt is short, like 20–40 tokens, completions about 120 tokens on average. but there are bursts during campaigns, so burst handling matters.
[00:48] Derek Morales: budget side — we have a soft constraint of $30k/mo for inference in the pilot bucket, and we'd like to see unit econ estimates so we can model scale.
[00:58] Devon Clarke: okay that helps. for those numbers, we usually look at two levers: batching to improve GPU utilization and prefix/KV caching to avoid recomputing common prefixes. on average, with 20–40 token prompts and 120 token responses, we see throughput improvements of ~2–3x with batching for gen workloads, and caching can reduce tokens generated for repeated context dramatically if you have repeated catalogue prefixes.
[01:22] Samir Patel: can you put some ballpark per-token numbers on the table now? just rough.
[01:26] Maria Santos: ballpark: on our hosted service with an open 13B-like model, baseline per-token infra cost is roughly $0.0008–$0.0012 per token without batching or caching; with batching and basic KV caching that often drops to $0.0003–$0.0006 per token depending on hit rate and quantization. vendor and model choices change that — higher perf models or quantized dedicated setups can be lower.
[01:54] Laura Chen: that range is pretty wide. how much does hit-rate matter for caching? we're likely to have ~30% prefix reuse across sessions.
[02:04] Devon Clarke: hit-rate is the biggest multiplier. with 30% prefix reuse, effective token savings end up reducing total token generation by about 20% end-to-end once you fold in generation overlap. with 60% reuse you're looking at maybe 35–45% fewer generated tokens.
[02:27] Priya Rao: under the hood, we care about latencies too. if we batch more aggressively, latency spikes. what knobs do you give us for latency vs cost?
[02:36] Devon Clarke: we expose batching window (ms), max batch size, and per-route SLO targets. you can tune batching window lower for p95 latency at the expense of throughput. also smart routing can fall back to a lower-cost model for non-critical calls.
[02:51] Samir Patel: so for the POC we should define success criteria — is it purely cost per 1M tokens and P95 latency? or product KPIs?
[02:59] Maria Santos: recommend both: (1) infra KPIs: p95 latency <= 200ms, availability >99.5 for the pilot routes, and cost per 1M tokens under $850 (that maps to your $30k/mo depending on usage). (2) product KPIs: search latency perceived <300ms and relevance uplift >10% over current baseline — we can help instrument that.
[03:22] Derek Morales: relevance uplift measurement, yes, we need an eval harness. can Redwood provide a template?
[03:27] Devon Clarke: yes, we have a bench template spreadsheet and eval harness script. we'll share it. it includes synthetic traffic generator, token accounting, latency measurement, and quality checks.
[03:37] Laura Chen: about the runner, we have strict infra policies. can you provide a containerized runner for on-prem benchmarking or does everything have to go through your hosted?
[03:48] Maria Santos: for POCs we can do either. we offer a lightweight containerized runner that executes local bench jobs and reports results back to the console; or you can point our hosted agents at a VPC endpoint. both are fine.
[04:00] Samir Patel: timeline — we're aiming to decide by end of quarter. can we do a 6-week pilot that proves unit economics and a benchmark results doc?
[04:08] Maria Santos: yes, a common cadence is a 6-week sprint: week 0 onboarding + dataset/prep, week 1 baseline runs, weeks 2–4 iterative tuning (batching, cache, quantize), week 5 production-like runs and analysis, week 6 final report and exec review.
[04:26] Priya Rao: security and compliance — we need SOC2 attestation and audit logs retained 90 days for the pilot. can you support that?
[04:34] Devon Clarke: hosted has SOC2 and audit logs; for VPC/private the control plane still provides logs and KMS integration. we'll share SOC2 report and the retention options.
[04:44] Samir Patel: what about competitor comparisons? we're evaluating a mix — OpenAI hosted, Anthropic for some models, and our internal self-host on GKE.
[04:54] Maria Santos: noted; Redwood can run head-to-heads with the models you care about. in our bench we can include OpenAI calls as a baseline for cost/latency.
[05:03] Derek Morales: actions — what do we need to provide?
[05:07] Maria Santos: sample traffic traces, a small representative dataset of queries, and a short list of high-priority product routes to test. also access for your infra folks if you want the on-prem runner.
[05:17] Laura Chen: I can get the traces and infra contact. timeline wise we can be ready in 10 days.
[05:22] Maria Santos: perfect. we'll send the bench template, a sample config for batching windows and caching TTLs, and a quote for the 6-week pilot.
[05:31] Devon Clarke: to be practical, for the bench we recommend testing three configurations: (A) low-latency: batching window 10ms, cache off; (B) balanced: batching window 40ms, cache with 30% hit-rate simulated; (C) cost-optimized: batching window 80–120ms, quantized model + cache hit-rate 60%. compare p95/p99, tokens generated, and per-1M-token cost.
[05:57] Samir Patel: for cost calc, can you show an example mapping from our numbers? say sustained 80qps, average 140 tokens total per request, 30 days.
[06:06] Devon Clarke: quick calc — sustained 80 qps * 140 tokens = 11,200 tokens/sec -> ~967M tokens/day -> ~29B tokens/month. at $0.0008/token that is $23,200/month; at $0.0004/token with caching/quantize that's $11,600/month. with your $30k pilot cap that gives headroom to run bursts and tests. these are rough and we'll provide a spreadsheet.
[06:40] Priya Rao: those monthly numbers are huge, we need to be confident caching and batching reduce total tokens.
[06:45] Maria Santos: agreed — the pilot's point is to empirically validate these deltas.
[06:50] Derek Morales: any hardware recommendations? we'll likely do a hybrid where sensitive traffic stays in our VPC.
[06:57] Devon Clarke: for dedicated capacity, we recommend 80–100GB A100-equivalent instances for the 13B-class model, but there are quantized configs that run on 48GB with some perf tradeoffs. we'll size the dedicated pool for your peak concurrency if you choose dedicated.
[07:14] Samir Patel: ok, next steps recap?
[07:16] Maria Santos: we'll: 1) share bench template + sample config, 2) send a pilot quote and contract terms, 3) provide the container runner and instructions if you want on-prem bench, 4) schedule infra deep-dive with Laura & Priya next week, and 5) run a quick smoke test once we get traces.
[07:31] Laura Chen: noted. I'll aim to have traces and infra contact within 10 days.
[07:36] Maria Santos: great. any other questions?
[07:39] Samir Patel: one more — how do you measure "relevance uplift" reproducibly?
[07:44] Devon Clarke: we use an A/B harness with holdout queries and a scoring function (MRR/recall@k) tied to your existing labels; can include human evals if needed. for the pilot we do automated offline evals and a small live A/B if you want.
[08:00] Derek Morales: sounds good. thanks all.
[08:03] Maria Santos: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and get the infra deep-dive on the calendar.
[47:00] -- call ends (note: timestamps in the body are approximate, transcription includes some noise and mis-attributions).
